prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands in twisted bilayer graphene at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in it

statement.case_for: I still prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene as a single-part prize, but I have changed one name. The discovery is a short, exactly stated prediction (the 2011 continuum model, with a flat band at a specific twist angle) followed by an experiment that found what the prediction made plausible: correlated insulators and superconductivity in 2018, reproduced by many independent groups, and a tunable platform for strongly correlated electrons that has since produced Chern-insulator and fractional states. A citation worded around the flat bands and the correlated phases does not rest on the pairing mechanism, which everyone agrees is unsettled. After reading the full exchange I credit Bistritzer rather than Andrei, because the prediction is a joint result and a prize that names the prediction should name both authors. The chair's summary shows no majority anywhere, so I am not reading the count as evidence of merit. I weigh B046 against B028 on one question, whether the credited names state who did the original work, and on that test B046 is cleaner than B028 once Bistritzer is in.
statement.case_against: Maturity is the weak point and I do not think the other members are wrong to say so. The key experiments are about eight years old, the pairing mechanism is debated, and twist-angle disorder makes sample-to-sample variation a real caveat. Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson would all hold B046 for a later year, and that is a defensible position, since nothing forces the prize this year. The attribution also still leaves out Cao, first author of the 2018 papers, and Andrei, whose earlier STM and transport work on twisted flat bands is real but did not predict the magic angle. B028 has fifteen to twenty years of confirmation and the broadest opening support, which is a serious reason to prefer it if the committee thinks timing outweighs clean credit. B034 is the cleanest in attribution but is closer to an instrument advance than to a new regime of matter.

responses.point: Eriksson argues that dropping Bistritzer misrepresents a prediction he co-authored, that the committee should credit contributions rather than seniority, and that Andrei's STM work did not predict the magic angle or see the correlated states.
responses.response: I accept this and I have changed my third name from Andrei to Bistritzer. My round-1 argument was that Bistritzer is already represented by the continuum-model credit given to MacDonald, but a credit names people, and the 2011 paper has two authors. Andrei's work showed twist-induced van Hove singularities and was independent evidence that something happens at small angles, yet it neither predicted the magic angle nor found the correlated phases. A prize for prediction plus discovery should name both authors of the prediction. The cost is that Andrei and Cao are left out, and I say so openly. This is the hardest cut in the configuration and I do not think the committee should hide it.

responses.point: Johansson calls B046 the stronger candidate for a later year, because it is about seven years old with the pairing mechanism unresolved and a four-name list for three slots, while B028 has two decades of confirmation. Johansson would still back B046 as second alternative if B028 stalls on credit.
responses.response: On the allocation problem I now think B046 is better placed than B028. Once the third slot is Bistritzer, the three names are exactly the two prediction authors and the experimental leader, and the only excluded claimants (Andrei, Cao) did supporting or follow-on work. In B028 the excluded claimants (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore, Balents) wrote theory that directly enabled the experiment and the 3D branch, so the credit would misstate more. On timing you are right and I do not dismiss it: seven to eight years is short. My view is that the open pairing mechanism is a reason for a careful citation, not for waiting. If the committee decides that timing outweighs credit, B028 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is my fallback, and I accept the 2D prediction-plus-HgTe citation over adding Hasan.

responses.point: Olsson says the credit for B028 is genuinely contested, since the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal and the Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents 3D theory cannot be represented, and that B034 is the cleaner configuration if the committee judges the prize would misstate who did the original work.
responses.response: I agree with the diagnosis and it is what moved my fallback order. If the committee decides B046 is too early, the choice is between B028 and B034. Your argument that B034 is cleaner on credit is correct, and I gave the same reason for ranking it third. I still disagree that cleanliness settles it, since the clock is an advance in precision of an established technique. Between the two fallbacks I stay with B028 first, because the intellectual gain, a new classification of band structure and its protected edge states, is larger, and I would accept the uncredited theorists as the price of a prize that names the 2D prediction and its first realisation.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that the 2005 comb prize overlaps with the lattice clock less than I suggested, because the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct scheme and Ye's credited contribution is the strontium clock realisation and its control of systematic shifts, not the comb. She also says a prize should not wait for an administrative redefinition of the second.
responses.response: I accept both points and I withdraw the comb-overlap objection as a main reason against B034. The magic-wavelength lattice is a new scheme, and I agree the discovery should not depend on when the metrology bodies act on the second. My remaining reservation is narrower: other lattice-clock groups (Lemonde, Ludlow, Lisdat, Bloom) have priority claims on early demonstrations that a two-name credit cannot reflect, and the physical gain is quantitative, orders of magnitude in accuracy and stability, not a new regime of matter. The same standard applies to my own candidate. If the committee accepts a clear prediction-and-experiment chain with some excluded claimants for B046, it should accept the same for B034, and I would then prefer it to B028 only if the credit for B028 cannot be worded honestly.

uncertainties: Whether eight years since the 2018 experiments is enough, given the unsettled pairing mechanism. This is the main reason B028 may be the better choice for this year.
Whether leaving out Andrei and Cao is acceptable. I rely on memory of the literature and have not checked priority dates beyond the supplied entries.
Whether the 2016 topological-phases prize reduces the claim of B028 as much as Lindroth believes, which would favour B046 or B034.
Whether the committee will accept my citation wording, which names the prediction and the correlated phases but not the pairing mechanism, as a faithful statement of what was discovered.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict is apparent from my profile for B046, B028 or B034. I have no documented connection to MacDonald, Bistritzer, Jarillo-Herrero, Andrei or any other credited name, and my own field, statistical physics of complex systems, is distant from moire materials. I note Kroll's disclosed possible proximity to the Hall laboratory environment for B034 and think it should be declared for the committee to weigh, as it was in round 1; I do not think it requires recusal.
